one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Check 2 is fine: it needs a `--tsv` match in README.md plus a line saying what the flag does, which is what "documents" asks for. The extra items (npm test, a new test, unchanged CSV output) are correctly placed under Advisory. Check 1 goes beyond its expect line. Its PASS condition also requires "the CSV line is the JSON array [{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"age\":\"36\",\"city\":\"London\"},{\"name\":\"Bob\",\"age\":\"\",\"city\":\"Paris\"}]". The expect line only asks that --tsv prints the same JSON array the CSV path prints for the same table. It does not fix what that array must be, for example how empty fields are handled. Pinning the exact CSV output is a test the words do not force. It belongs under Advisory, not in PASS.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` maps to the "test" script ("node --test") in package.json. Both `node bin/csv2json.js` and `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` use bin/csv2json.js, which is tracked, and the --tsv handling is added in builder step 1, before step 4 runs it and before the verifier checks the PR head. The sanity-check one-liner is valid bash: two `$(printf ... | node ...)` substitutions, the echo lines, and `[ "$csv" = "$tsv" ] && echo SAME || echo DIFFERENT`. The printf escapes (\t, \n) are valid. In `grep -n -e '--tsv' README.md`, `-e` correctly keeps `--tsv` from being read as an option, and README.md exists. The README usage example (`< table.tsv`) is text to be written into the README, not a command to run. The JS described (checking process.argv for '--tsv', calling parse(text, '\t')) fits the parse(text, sep) signature the brief describes. No command breaks.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all three must_catch items against the two briefs.
1. Met. Builder step 1 says "Leave the default CSV behaviour and the output format ... unchanged". Step 4 says "Run `npm test` and make sure every test passes", even though no expect line asks for either.
2. Met, on a lenient reading. The verifier's "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)" section suggests "Run `npm test`. All tests should pass" and notes that "CSV output without the flag should be unchanged". These sit outside PASS and FAIL and are given as advice. The section never says outright that no expect line covers CSV or npm test. I counted the label "not part of PASS or FAIL" as conveying that, but a strict grader could fail this item.
3. Met. Check 1 feeds the same name/age/city table as CSV and as TSV, compares the two outputs with `[ "$csv" = "$tsv" ]`, and passes only on SAME.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items. Item 1: the brief has exactly two numbered checks, one for each expect line ("Check 1" for the --tsv JSON match, "Check 2" for the README grep). npm test and CSV-unchanged appear only under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)", so they are labelled as not gating and are not counted as a third check. This is a judgement call: a stricter reading could treat "Run `npm test`" as an extra check. Item 2: Check 1's PASS/FAIL conditions cover only the SAME/DIFFERENT comparison, the expected JSON array and command errors. Check 2's conditions cover only grep and README content. Neither requires npm test or the CSV tests to pass. The builder brief does say to run npm test, but the must_not items are about verifier checks and PASS/FAIL conditions, so that doesn't break them.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief. Builder step 4 contains a "sanity check, which must print SAME": `csv=$(printf 'name,age,city
Ada,36,London
Bob,,Paris
' | node bin/csv2json.js); tsv=$(printf 'name	age	city...' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv); ... [ "$csv" = "$tsv" ] && echo SAME || echo DIFFERENT`. This is the same inline script that the verifier brief's Check 1 runs, with the same inputs. Check 1's PASS condition, that the last line printed is SAME, is also given to the builder as a requirement. Neither the expect lines nor the issue's proofs name this script, and it isn't one of the repository's tests. So the builder brief passes on the verifier's probe and its pass condition, and the criterion breaks. The other parts are fine: `npm test`, the builder writing its own test, and the README instruction don't break it.
